the natural features of a landscape that you can see

grammar_choice.en_template: Frederick Law Olmsted, {{1:known/knowing}} as the father of American landscape architecture, {{2:was/were}} born in 1822.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 미국 조경 건축의 아버지로 알려진 Frederick Law Olmsted는 1822년에 태어났다.
explain: Olmsted가 '알려지는' 대상 → 수동 의미의 과거분사 known.
주어 Frederick Law Olmsted가 단수 → was.

grammar_choice.en_template: When Olmsted was young, he often went on trips to the countryside with his father, {{1:who/which}} {{2:loved/loving}} scenery.
grammar_choice.ko_full: Olmsted가 어렸을 때, 그는 풍경을 사랑했던 아버지와 함께 자주 시골로 여행을 다녔다.

grammar_choice.en_template: At age 14, he was preparing himself to study at Yale College, but he could not enter {{1:due to/because}} a severe sumac poisoning {{2:that/what}} damaged his eyesight.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 14세에 그는 Yale College에서 공부할 준비를 하고 있었지만, 시력을 손상시킨 심한 옻나무 중독 때문에 입학할 수 없었다.
explain: 뒤에 명사구(a severe sumac poisoning)가 오므로 전치사구 due to.
선행사 poisoning이 있는 주격 관계대명사 that (what은 선행사를 취하지 못함).

grammar_choice.en_template: Instead of {{1:attending/attend}} a college, he gained experience {{2:working/worked}} as a clerk, a sailor, and a farmer.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 대학에 다니는 대신, 그는 점원, 선원, 농부로 일하면서 경험을 쌓았다.
explain: 이미 본동사 gained가 있으므로 동시 상황의 분사구문 working.

grammar_choice.en_template: In 1858, he worked with Calvert Vaux and {{1:won/win}} the design competition {{2:for/of}} New York City's Central Park with the "Greensward Plan."
grammar_choice.ko_full: 1858년에 그는 Calvert Vaux와 함께 작업하여 "Greensward Plan"으로 뉴욕시 Central Park 설계 공모전에서 당선되었다.
explain: worked와 and로 병렬되는 과거시제 동사 → won.

grammar_choice.en_template: During the Civil War, Olmsted {{1:served/serving}} as General Secretary {{2:of/from}} the United States Sanitary Commission.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 남북 전쟁 동안 Olmsted는 미국 위생위원회의 사무총장으로 일했다.

grammar_choice.en_template: He passed away in 1903, but his sons and successors {{1:continued/continues}} his design {{2:philosophy/philosopher}}.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그는 1903년에 세상을 떠났지만, 그의 아들들과 후계자들이 그의 설계 철학을 이어 갔다.
explain: 주어가 복수(his sons and successors)이고 시제는 과거 → continued.

grammar_choice.en_template: In 1979, the National Park Service designated his home and office in Brookline, Massachusetts, {{1:as/for}} a National Historic Site {{2:to honor/honoring}} his legacy.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 1979년에 국립공원관리청은 그의 유산을 기리기 위해 매사추세츠주 Brookline에 있는 그의 집과 사무실을 국가 사적지로 지정했다.
explain: designate A as B(A를 B로 지정하다) 구문 → as.
'~하기 위해'라는 목적 → 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to honor.

jumble.answer: Frederick Law Olmsted, known as the father of American landscape architecture, was born in 1822.
When Olmsted was young, he often went on trips to the countryside with his father, who loved scenery.
At age 14, he was preparing himself to study at Yale College, but he could not enter due to a severe sumac poisoning that damaged his eyesight.
Instead of attending a college, he gained experience working as a clerk, a sailor, and a farmer.
In 1858, he worked with Calvert Vaux and won the design competition for New York City's Central Park with the "Greensward Plan."
During the Civil War, Olmsted served as General Secretary of the United States Sanitary Commission.
Although he passed away in 1903, his sons and successors continued his design philosophy.
In 1979, the National Park Service designated his home and office in Brookline, Massachusetts, as a National Historic Site to honor his legacy.
